headline: Chips Drag a Lopsided Friday Close; Traders Eye Geopolitics and Fed Signals Heading Into September
body_html:
Friday's session handed the bears a narrow but telling victory. Of the 549 names in our universe, 353 finished lower against just 193 advancing — a ratio that tells most of the story before a single sector figure is read. Semiconductors bore the brunt, shedding 3.49% as a group, with Marvell Technology falling 10.28%, Semtech off 7.91%, and both FormFactor and Onto Innovation dropping roughly 7.5%. The selloff rippled into adjacent hardware and power-module names, underscoring how quickly sentiment in the AI supply chain can sour when a single earnings signal disappoints.

Not everything surrendered. Homebuilders added 0.85% to lead all sectors, and Consumer names edged up 0.34%. Gap Inc. surged 12.94% after results that apparently reassured investors the brand-restructuring effort is gaining traction. Specialty-chemicals firm Solstice Advanced Materials matched that energy with a 12.76% gain. Schlumberger climbed 4.22%, a notable bright spot in an Energy sector that itself dipped 0.26% on the day.

The week ahead arrives loaded with macro and geopolitical crosscurrents. Iran's assertion of control over the Strait of Hormuz — following a six-month conflict that has already prompted QatarEnergy to suspend gas deliveries to European buyers — keeps energy-supply risk front of mind. Domestically, Federal Reserve chair-in-waiting Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks will be parsed for any shift in rate-path guidance, even as the CBOE volatility index touched its lowest mark of the year. Markets that are calm on paper are not always calm underneath.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Rout Puts AI Hardware Names on Watch
briefs.body: Friday's chip wreckage — led by double-digit losses in Marvell Technology and steep declines across equipment and analog names — raises pointed questions about near-term demand visibility in the AI buildout. Investors will be scrutinising any fresh data-center order commentary from suppliers in the week ahead for confirmation that the selloff was idiosyncratic rather than cyclical.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Threat Adds a Premium to Energy Markets
briefs.body: Iran's navy declared full operational control over the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint through which a significant share of global oil and LNG transits daily. That assertion, combined with fresh US sanctions on Egyptian bank branches linked to Iranian transactions, is likely to keep an energy-supply risk premium alive as traders return Monday.

briefs.headline: QatarEnergy Halt Tightens European Gas Supply Picture
briefs.body: QatarEnergy's decision to suspend gas deliveries to Italy's Edison through early November — citing the ongoing Iran conflict — removes a meaningful volume from an already tight European market heading into autumn. The move echoes broader supply-chain disruptions that analysts warn could widen if the six-month-old conflict escalates further.

briefs.headline: Warsh Debut at Jackson Hole Sets the Tone for Rate Watchers
briefs.body: Traders are growing more comfortable with Kevin Warsh as the anticipated next Fed chair, with the volatility index settling at a year-to-date low even as his Jackson Hole address landed. Market participants will spend the coming days parsing his remarks on inflation tolerance and the pace of any policy normalisation, making Fed-speak the dominant domestic macro theme.

briefs.headline: Gap's Blowout Session Signals Consumer-Apparel Resilience
briefs.body: Gap Inc. rocketed 12.94% on Friday, the strongest single-session gain in our universe, after results suggested the retailer's multiyear restructuring is delivering. The move lifts spirits in a Consumer sector that has otherwise been treading water, and it will focus attention on any forward guidance commentary the company offers in follow-up investor meetings this week.

briefs.headline: Meta's Settlement Reshapes Platform Accountability Landscape
briefs.body: A landmark settlement requiring Meta to implement new child-safety safeguards — valued at roughly 17 billion dollars — is drawing scrutiny from platform-accountability advocates who call the promised measures meaningful but incomplete. The agreement sets a precedent that other large consumer-internet platforms may now be forced to reckon with in their own regulatory negotiations.
